G2-S1-A: Make your brand easy to understand and easy to verify. Keep the same clear facts about who you are everywhere, publish pages that answer real buyer questions directly, allow AI search crawlers to read your site and earn mentions on sites AI tools already trust. Then check what assistants say every month.
G2-S1-NOGUARANTEE: Nobody can guarantee that ChatGPT, or any other AI assistant, will cite your brand. Not us, not an agency, not a tool. Nobody controls what assistants say, so anyone selling a guaranteed citation is selling something they can't deliver.
G2-S2-H2: How ChatGPT finds and chooses sources
G2-S2-A: It draws on pages its search crawler is allowed to read. OpenAI says sites that opt out of its OAI-SearchBot crawler won't be shown in ChatGPT search answers, apart from plain navigational links. It doesn't publish how sources are then chosen, so clear, direct pages that other sites back up are your best bet.
G2-S3-H2: Step 1: Check what AI says about you today
G2-S3-A: Ask it the questions your customers would ask, such as "best skincare brands for sensitive skin in the UK" or "who can help a clinic get more reviews". Record whether you're named and which sources it cites. Repeat monthly with the same prompts in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI results.

G2-S10-H2: Can I pay to be listed in ChatGPT?
G2-S10-A: Not as a citation. OpenAI's crawler documentation lists OAI-AdsBot, which checks the safety of pages submitted as ads on ChatGPT. But an ad is a paid placement, not your brand being cited in an answer, and nobody can sell you a guaranteed citation. Check OpenAI's current ads information before you spend anything.
G2-FAQ-H2: Questions about getting cited by AI
G2-FAQ-1-Q: How long does it take to get mentioned by AI assistants?
G2-FAQ-1-A: There's no reliable timescale, and anyone who quotes one is guessing. Changes to your site have to be crawled again, and mentions on other sites take time to earn. Set checkpoints, run the same prompts each month and judge progress by the trend over several months, not by a single answer.
G2-FAQ-2-Q: Does ChatGPT use Google or Bing to find sources?
G2-FAQ-2-A: OpenAI's crawler documentation doesn't say, so we won't guess. What it does say is that ChatGPT search shows sites its OAI-SearchBot crawler is allowed to read. So allow that crawler, open your pages with clear answers and earn genuine mentions elsewhere. Those steps are worth doing whichever index sits behind it.
G2-FAQ-3-A: Only if you're happy to drop out of those tools' search results. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot won't be shown in ChatGPT search answers. Perplexity recommends allowing PerplexityBot to appear in its results. Training is a separate choice: you can block OpenAI's GPTBot on its own.
G2-FAQ-4-Q: Do reviews matter for AI answers?
G2-FAQ-4-A: They can help. Genuine reviews on trusted platforms are one way other sites back up what you say about yourself, which may make your brand easier to trust. Nobody outside these companies knows exactly how much they count. Ask real customers, never pay for reviews and follow Google's review policy.
G2-FAQ-5-A: The basics are the same. Perplexity says PerplexityBot is designed to surface and link websites in its search results, and it recommends allowing it in your robots.txt. So the same steps apply: clear facts, answer-first pages, open access for its crawler and genuine mentions elsewhere.
